newsitem.title: FRANCE: Current European FX parities correct - Lamfalussy.
newsitem.headline: Current European FX parities correct - Lamfalussy.

text.p: Alexandre Lamfalussy, head of the European Monetary Institute, said parities between the major European currencies, including the franc and the mark, were correct, afternoon daily Le Monde reported on Thursday.
"The parities overall - not only between the franc and the mark -- seem to me correct," he said in an interview.

"As for the franc, whatever indices we look at, its bilateral exchange rate compared to the mark, or the effective real rate compared to the group of currencies, we see for years a great stability. We can even see a certain improvement in the competitiveness of the country. I really do not see a problem.
Lamfalussy went on to say the dollar remained undervalued compared to major European currencies.
"At its current level compared to the principal European currencies, the dollar seems to me still undervalued," he told the newspaper.
He said the United States could get away with a weak dollar because of the currency's role as a reserve and international payment currency.

"If we want to make the euro a true alternative in international financial marketplaces, the euro must have credibility and stability. This depends on the policies followed for the euro," Lamfalussy said.
"To the extent that the European Central Bank can effectively follow a policy of price stability and create a zone of internal stability, the currency will acquire a very great strength," he said.

"The Americans will no longer be able to allow themselves to have periods of weakness in their currency. They would risk a downward slippage, with, as a consequence, problems on the workings of their markets, rises in long term interest rates.
"And at that time, monetary authorities in the United States, and maybe budgetary authorities will have to change the policy mix," he said.
